abstract_title: Cancer Detection in Histopathological Images and Explainable AI (XAI) Supported Decision System
abstract_text: Histopathological examination, considered the gold standard in cancer diagnosis, is undergoing a transformation that necessitates AI integration due to observer-dependent variability and workload of manual evaluation. This project aims to develop an explainable AI system capable of analyzing multiple cancer types using five open datasets containing over 530,000 histopathological images of breast, lung, and colon cancers. All models were trained using EfficientNet-based transfer learning, with images processed through a standard preprocessing pipeline. The breast cancer model was progressively specialized through a three-stage transfer learning strategy. On the IDC dataset, 82% accuracy was achieved; in the second stage with transfer to BACH, 94%; and in the final BreakHis model, 87% accuracy and 0.90 ROC-AUC metrics were reached, with cancer sensitivity at 0.95 especially in malignant tissues. The model developed for lymph node metastasis of breast cancer achieved 95% accuracy. Lung and colon models reached 100% accuracy, and validating the generalizability of this performance with new datasets is a recommended approach in literature. Grad-CAM-based explainable AI (XAI) was integrated as a core component, providing visual heat maps showing which tissue regions the model focuses on for decisions. This approach aims not only to achieve high accuracy but also to make AI model predictions transparent and assist expert physicians in their evaluations. The project was developed into a concrete software product with a web application and API for external integration, offering image upload, classification, and Grad-CAM outputs on a single platform. In conclusion, the project presents a scientific AI model with R&D character and a prototype AI assistant usable for clinical preliminary evaluation.
